matches.rationale: Both ground truth and finding identify the exact same issue with Equation (1) in Section 4.1: the incorrect application of ISVD with improperly defined orthogonal matrices P_k^{(i)} and Q^{(i)}, breaking the reconstruction logic. The supporting evidence in pred_id 1 is verbatim from the ground truth.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same issue with Equation (5): the ill-formed matrix multiplication of row vector e_{i,j}^T with U_k^{(i)} and ambiguous notation for leverage score computation. The supporting evidence in pred_id 2 matches the ground truth exactly.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same experimental design issue in Section 5.1: lack of clarity on replay buffer budget M enforcement across clients, sample allocation under heterogeneity, and insufficient baseline comparison details. The supporting evidence in pred_id 3 is identical to the ground truth.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same data integrity issue in Tables 2 and 3: missing standard deviation/variance measures for TinyImageNet results, limiting assessment of stability and statistical significance. The supporting evidence in pred_id 4 matches the ground truth.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same claim distortion in Section 5.2: exaggerated interpretation of 'adaptability and robustness' based on uneven and sometimes marginal improvements, without quantifying computational overhead or analyzing failure cases. The supporting evidence in pred_id 5 is identical.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same reference fabrication issue: citations [5], [6], [8], [12], [13] refer to future conferences/journals beyond knowledge cutoff or unverifiable papers, undermining scholarly reliability. The supporting evidence in pred_id 6 matches exactly.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same ethical integrity omission: lack of statements about ethical approval, consent, or privacy risks in federated learning settings throughout the Experiments section. The supporting evidence in pred_id 7 is identical to the ground truth.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same rhetorical manipulation in the Abstract: overpromising language about achieving balanced sampling and improved generalization without qualifiers about limitations, inflating contributions beyond modest accuracy gains. The supporting evidence in pred_id 8 matches exactly.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same context misalignment in the Conclusion: asserting FedCBDR 'effectively reduces imbalance and significantly improves performance' without acknowledging limitations, marginal improvements, or parameter sensitivity from earlier sections. The supporting evidence in pred_id 9 is identical.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same data integrity issue in Tables 2, 3, and 5: selective omission of variance for some baselines (especially TinyImageNet), inconsistent rounding, and underreporting of competing methods in challenging cases. The supporting evidence in pred_id 10 matches exactly.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same method logic inconsistency in Section 4.2 and equations (7) and (9): inconsistent application of temperature scaling factors τ_old and τ_new, unclear shape/concatenation of logits, and ambiguous relation to weighting parameters. The supporting evidence in pred_id 11 is identical.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same claim distortion in Section 5.3: overemphasis on TTS module's 'consistent improvements' when Table 4 shows marginal gains within standard deviations, without accounting for variance or negative results. The supporting evidence in pred_id 12 matches exactly.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same experimental protocol issue in Section 5.1: omission of computational budgets, training duration, and tuning methodology for baselines, especially costly methods like LANDER, impairing reproducibility and fair comparison. The supporting evidence in pred_id 13 is identical.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same data integrity issue in Section 5.6: selective reporting in hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, excluding poor-performing settings (e.g., extreme τ_new values), biasing interpretation and overstating robustness. The supporting evidence in pred_id 14 matches exactly.

Both ground truth and finding identify the same context misalignment between Abstract and Method: Abstract claims 'global coordination mechanism' implying comprehensive global view, but Method reveals only encrypted pseudo features with privacy/dimensionality constraints, overstating global insight capability. The supporting evidence in pred_id 15 is identical.
